title: Weight-Space Programming for Vision–Language Model Repair

notes_for_review: A careful audit showing that LLM-agent repair of planted VLM faults largely exploits a numerical artifact: float32 fault arithmetic leaves nonzero low bits on BF16 weights, and removing that trace (rounding) removes most of the repair. Includes random-edit controls, a placebo-hint control, fixed scripts, and Adam/LoRA fits, with weight-by-weight audit against clean checkpoints; the main hint test on six checkpoints gives a 19.01-point paired gain over placebo. Small sample sizes and many single-session conditions; the paper's methodological recommendation (report number format, include a rounded control) applies to other planted-fault WSP studies.
